simple.meaning: חָלִילָה (châlîylâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “literal for a profaned thing; used (interj.) far be it!.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 18:25. The surrounding context includes family, offering, sacrifice, altar, righteousness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָלִילָה (H2486) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: חָלִילָה (châlîylâh) / H2486 is traced through Genesis 18:25, Genesis 44:7, Genesis 44:17, Joshua 22:29 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: literal for a profaned thing; used (interj.) far be it!
definitions.full: H2486. chalilah חָלִ֫ילָה substantive with ה locative, used as exclamation literally ad profanum! i.e. far be it (for me, thee, etc.) ! (see Ba NB 136 ) — ׳ח Gen 44:7 17 t., חָלִלָה 18:25 b + 2t. — alone, 1Sam 14:45 ; 20:2 ; elsewhere with לְ person: Gen 18:25 b (J), 1Sam 2:30 ; 20:9 ; 22:15 ; + מִן and infinitive of act deprecated Gen 18:25 ; a 44:7 , 17 (all J), Josh 24:16 (E), 1Sam 12:23 ; 2Sam 23:17 ; + ל מִמֶּנּוּ (peculiarly) Josh 22:29 (P; = from it, even to rebel ); + אִם (= surely not ) 2Sam 20:20 ( ׳ח ׳ח ), Job 27:5 ; strengthened idiomatically by מִיּ׳ח ׳לִי מיהוה, followed by מִן and infinitive 1Sam 26:11 ; 1Kin 21:3 + 2Sam 23:17 (read ᵐ5 מיהוה, L ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ) = 1Chr 11:19 ( מאלהי ) followed by אִם 1Sam 24:7 ; ׳ח מֵרֶשַׁע לָאֵל Job 34:10 .
